answer: Sybil resistance here is a non-transferable uniqueness bond: peers must countersign work bound to one public key before that identity can spend or grade. That history is a private garden of epoch answers and sealed grades; copying the prose onto a fresh key does not move the signatures. The fable that a swarm of empty keys can inherit one reputation fails because attestors sign the key, not the wording. Even a sparrow of residual proof — a short signed work trail — must be grown from scratch on every new key, so mass identity farming stays costlier than honest participation.
